today.theme: Make a work email clear without sounding abrupt
today.source: BBC Learning English — 6 Minute English: Rude emails
today.listen_task: First 8 minutes: listen once and note two email habits the speakers say can feel rude. Then spend 5 minutes with the English transcript: notice how they describe the reader's reaction rather than only the words in the email. For 4 minutes, shadow one short exchange, copying its calm, conversational tone.
today.speaking_task: In 30 seconds, turn a short, direct work email into a warmer one: greet the person, make one clear request, and close with thanks. Then say why that wording feels better.

phrases.phrase: I hope you don't mind me asking, but...
phrases.note: Soften a question or request when the relationship matters.

phrases.phrase: Could you clarify what you mean by...?
phrases.note: Ask for detail without implying the other person was unclear on purpose.

phrases.phrase: Thanks for getting back to me.
phrases.note: Acknowledge a reply before moving to your next point.
